Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education | National No institution, including UG, is above the law – Acting Rent Commissioner Source : Prince Adu-Owusu 18 November 2026 5:50pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Acting Rent Control Commissioner Frederick Opoku has defended his decision to inspect hostel facilities operated by the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), insisting that no institution is above the laws of the country.
He said the inspection was part of efforts to protect students from poor accommodation conditions and ensure that landlords and property managers complied with rent regulations.
Speaking on JoyNews ’ The Pulse on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Opoku said he had formally notified the university's management of complaints about the state of its hostel facilities before undertaking the inspection.
He rejected suggestions that he had been provoked into confronting the hostel manager, arguing that institutions must respect the authority of the law and engage with regulatory bodies when jurisdictional concerns arise.
“I don't think I was provoked because for me from my side, I believe that we are all somehow officers and we must respect each other.
“We must respect our limits and be obedient to the laws of the Republic. I always say no institution, including Legon can be more than or bigger than the laws of the Republic. And where an institution believes they have some jurisdiction, we need to talk,” he said.
Mr Opoku explained that the visit was an inspection prompted by reports about the poor maintenance of the facilities, adding that the university had been informed beforehand.
He said the Rent Control Department had been inspecting hostels across the country and that UGEL was not being singled out.
“This was an inspection. That I have received something and students genuinely across the country - you saw me moving around a lot of hostels.
“So you are not the first, and you will never be the last,” he said.
The Acting Rent Control Commissioner further accused some property managers of taking advantage of students, who he said often struggle to speak up about poor accommodation conditions.
He cited concerns about mould, rodents and other maintenance issues, arguing that students should not be left exposed to such conditions simply because their accommodation is operated by a university institution.
“That's why I thought it is not right because the students seem voiceless and they cannot talk. And because they are under you, you believe that you can do whatever pleases you. We think it is not good,” he added.
Mr Opoku nearly got into a physical altercation with a hostel manager during an inspection of facilities operated by UGEL at the University of Ghana.
The confrontation reportedly followed a disagreement between the two during the inspection.
In a video of the incident, the hostel manager is heard telling the Acting Rent Commissioner, “President Mahama will not like what you are doing.”
Mr Opoku responded, “You are stealing money, and you said, President Mahama.”
“I said go to court, go and tell your boss,” he added angrily.
The incident is the latest in a series of confrontations involving the Acting Rent Commissioner during nationwide inspections aimed at enforcing rent regulations.
His enforcement activities have reportedly resulted in disagreements with some landlords and property managers over compliance with the country's rent laws.
